title: Hospital performance and operational review
objective: Produce a reproducible monthly performance review using encounter and medication-order extracts.
business_request: The COO says General Medicine appears to have longer stays and medication workload is increasing. Confirm what the data show, identify data-quality risks, and recommend what management should investigate next.
clarifications: What is the reporting period and date field?
Is the encounter row the unit of analysis?
How is readmission_30d_flag defined and validated?
Does medication order volume mean unique order lines, active orders, or administrations?
Should missing cost be excluded or estimated? Never impute without approval.
tasks: Profile row counts, keys, date ranges, missingness and invalid values.
Define a metric dictionary with grain, numerator, denominator and exclusions.
Calculate monthly encounters, mean and median LOS, supplied readmission flag proportion and order lines per encounter.
Compare departments while describing case-mix and data completeness.
Reconcile orphan orders and missing unit costs.
Prepare an executive dashboard specification and one-page findings memo.
acceptance: All source rows accounted for; no silent deletion.
Encounter and order grains explicitly separated.
Every KPI has formula and denominator.

title: Antihypertensive DUE and clinical pharmacy review
objective: Demonstrate a defensible drug utilisation evaluation using synthetic records.
business_request: The committee wants to understand antihypertensive prescribing patterns and whether available blood pressure documentation can support a descriptive review.
clarifications: What constitutes an eligible encounter and antihypertensive order?
Are repeated encounters from one patient included?
Are orders active, completed, or discontinued?
Is SBP baseline/follow-up measured in comparable time windows?
Which dated guideline and local formulary should be used for concordance? No guideline claims without a source.
tasks: Define DUE population, unit of analysis and exclusions.
Filter antihypertensive class; summarise order lines and generic-name patterns.
Describe single vs multiple order lines only if data support the definition.
Assess missing baseline/follow-up SBP and calculate paired change only among complete pairs.
Separate prescribing patterns from BP outcomes and state data limitations.
deliverables: Cleaned analytical dataset and reproducible script
Clinical interpretation with references to be added by analyst
acceptance: No claim of administration, dispensing or adherence from order rows.
Paired SBP analysis uses matched records and reports n.
No guideline concordance conclusion without dated authoritative criteria.
Missing data and selection limitations reported.

title: Remote client request-to-handoff
objective: Simulate remote analyst delivery from ambiguous request through scoped, validated handoff.
business_request: A client sends a service-ticket export and asks: 'Show whether our support is getting faster and tell us which team is underperforming.'
clarifications: What does faster mean: first response, resolution, or time to closure?
Which timestamp represents receipt and which represents completion?
How should open tickets be treated?
Are priority and client type comparable across teams?
What time zone and business-hours calendar apply?
What is the minimum cell size for reporting?
tasks: Write a concise clarification note and assumptions log.
Profile timestamp ordering, missing closure times and status consistency.
Calculate elapsed clock hours for closed tickets; do not label as business hours.
Summarise median and 90th percentile closure time by priority and client type with counts.
Draft client-ready summary, limitations and next steps.
deliverables: Client handoff memo and QA checklist
acceptance: Open tickets not treated as zero-duration closed tickets.
Clock hours distinguished from business hours.
Small groups flagged; no unsupported team blame.
Handoff includes files, refresh date, validation and known limitations.
